svg.text: Calling introgressions with k-mers (no read mapping)
one 100-kb window of the B73 genome · one sequenced sample = a pool of 6 BC2S3 plants from one plot
Cut the B73 reference genome (RefGen v5) into every 31-letter word (k-mer). Keep only words that occur ONCE.
single-copy k-mer: kept (680 M of 817 M)
repeat k-mer: dropped (present in every genome)
Look the k-mers up in each sample's reads (step 17)
Count all k-mers in the sample's raw reads (KMC). Reads are never mapped, so donor reads are not lost.
every B73 k-mer that a read covers is found
k-mers that overlap a donor SNP or indel are missing
r = k-mers found in the pool ÷ k-mers our sequenced B73 control samples find at the same depth. Expected DONOR level d: from the teosinte
assemblies to start with, then learned from all our pools of the taxon (our donor plants are not the assembly plants).
Our sequenced B73 controls find ~30% at
DONOR: the Zd genome has only 27% of
these k-mers, so the pool finds ~2,600:
SEG: shared k-mers (27%) are found as usual;
the rest come only from the B73 half,
Where the teosinte keeps most B73 k-mers, count only the informative ones
There (e.g. parviglumis chr7 54-65 Mb, 90% kept) the shared k-mers are found in every pool, whatever its state: they add noise, no signal.
Informative k-mers of a taxon = B73 single-copy k-mers found in NONE of the taxon's assemblies. Pools are counted against their taxon's list too.
shared with the teosinte: found in every pool
informative: in no assembly, only from B73 DNA
A window uses its informative k-mers if B73 has at least 200 of them there and the DONOR/SEG contrast rises at least 1.2× (33-53% of measured windows,
by taxon); its DONOR level and spread then come from our pools called DONOR there. Contrast = the SEG-DONOR gap in noise units
Windows → B73 / SEG / DONOR. Switches follow the NAM genetic map; switch rate ρ fitted by maximum likelihood.
